records.transaction_or_state_machine_analysis: LISTENING -> CLOSING has unowned entry paths, and REQUEST_ACTIVE has no cancellation relation to CLOSING. A rejection can escape without moving the API to FAILED/CLOSED.
records.root_cause: Listener, request, logging, and close resources are composed as independent promises rather than one lifecycle-owned abort/error boundary.
records.minimal_fix_boundary: Install error/signal ownership before listen is exposed, wrap every async request path, assign an idempotent close promise before fallible work, track sockets and requests, abort/stop admission on close, apply an aggregate deadline, and settle closed with a recorded success/failure exactly once.
required_tests: Throwing metrics/status/cockpit/logger callbacks
Open keep-alive and partial-body requests during SIGTERM
Concurrent close calls and two signals
server.close error and timeout
Request completion after replacement generation starts
application.closed resolution/rejection contract
regression_risks: Force-closing sockets can truncate legitimate read responses; define grace then abort
Changing closed rejection semantics affects CLI error propagation
aliases_or_dependencies: BWS116-R03-005 owns psql cancellation; BWS116-R03-011 owns scheduler/worker in-flight cancellation
explicitly_unchanged_areas: Loopback-only bind and GET-only query policy remain unchanged
No non-loopback network was contacted

records.title: Successful service passes leave timeout timers alive until their full configured duration
records.relevant_lifecycle_object_or_process: Per-pass timeout timer and Node event-loop liveness

source_evidence.note: Promise.race creates a sleep timer and never clears/unrefs it when the pass resolves first.
Scheduler has the same timer ownership pattern.
Worker has the same timer ownership pattern.

records.preconditions: A pass resolves before passTimeoutMs, including maxPasses=1 tests or shutdown after a quick pass.
records.trigger: Run a fast pass with a multi-second timeout and allow the service function to return.
records.expected_behavior: The losing timeout branch must be cancelled and released immediately, or use an unrefed/abortable deadline that cannot hold process liveness.
records.current_behavior: Every successful pass leaves its timer pending. Repeated passes accumulate active timers; the final one can keep Node alive after the function returns.
records.impact: Shutdown and test processes are delayed, timer count grows with pass rate, and outer lifecycle timeouts can expire after logical completion.
records.evidence: The inert worker harness returned in 21.64 ms with a 2500 ms pass timeout, but process wall time exceeded the control by about 2.30 seconds, matching the pending timer.

reproduction_status.result: Function completed quickly; process remained alive until losing timeout timer expired.

records.transaction_or_state_machine_analysis: PASS_COMPLETED releases business work but not the timeout resource. Resource cleanup is not coupled to the race settlement.
records.root_cause: The timeout helper uses a bare sleep promise whose timer handle is inaccessible to the winner path.
records.minimal_fix_boundary: Replace sleepFor race with an abortable timeout helper that clears its handle in finally, and ensure late pass handling remains owned under the R01/R03 cancellation contracts.
required_tests: Fast pass with long timeout
Thousands of quick passes with active-handle count
Shutdown immediately after pass completion
Timeout winner and pass rejection races
No double settlement or unhandled rejection
regression_risks: Do not accidentally stop observing the underlying pass when the timeout wins
Timer unref alone does not solve late work ownership
aliases_or_dependencies: Distinct from BWS116-R01-007 and BWS116-R03-011: those own uncancelled underlying work, while this finding owns the losing timer handle
explicitly_unchanged_areas: Pass classification semantics remain unchanged
No provider or database work was executed

records.title: Unexpected pass failures exit without a terminal service state or failure evidence
records.relevant_lifecycle_object_or_process: Standalone service state/evidence on unclassified pass rejection

source_evidence.note: The loop has try/finally only for listener disposal; an unexpected pass rejection escapes after running state/pass-start state is written.
Scheduler has the same no-catch terminal-state path.
Worker has the same no-catch terminal-state path.

records.preconditions: An injected or production pass promise rejects instead of returning the expected BoundaryResult, or a state/evidence/log write throws.
records.trigger: Reject the pass promise after service_started and pass-start state are written.
records.expected_behavior: The service must transition to failed/unknown with timestamp, error class, current pass, process generation, and terminal evidence before returning/rethrowing; status must not report running.
records.current_behavior: The rejection escapes. Signal listeners are disposed, but the durable state remains lifecycleState=running and no failure/stop evidence is written.
records.impact: Status and metrics can falsely report a dead service as running; restart sees stale state without the failure cause; incident evidence is incomplete.
records.evidence: The inert worker harness rejected one pass. It returned an error while state remained running, totalPassCount=0, hasLastPass=false, and only the service_started evidence existed.

reproduction_status.result: Rejected pass left durable state running with no terminal failure evidence.

records.transaction_or_state_machine_analysis: RUNNING -> PASS_STARTED -> exception has no transition. The process exits, but durable state remains at the prior nonterminal node.
records.root_cause: Only expected result variants are modeled; unexpected exceptions are treated as process errors without durable lifecycle finalization.
records.minimal_fix_boundary: Add failed/unknown terminal states and a top-level catch/finally that records sanitized failure evidence and state exactly once, while preserving the original error and any ambiguous in-flight operation identity.
required_tests: Rejected pass promise
State write failure after pass
Evidence/logger failure after state write
Exception during classification
Restart/status from failed and unknown states
regression_risks: Failure finalization itself can fail and needs a bounded fallback record
Do not misclassify a timed-out but still-running pass as safely failed
aliases_or_dependencies: BWS116-R03-011 owns cancellation of in-flight scheduler/worker work; this finding owns durable service terminality after an exception
explicitly_unchanged_areas: Expected BoundaryResult blocker/retry outcomes remain unchanged
No persistent state outside the disposable harness was written

records.title: Millisecond evidence filenames collide across legitimate lifecycle events and can crash the service
records.relevant_lifecycle_object_or_process: Immutable lifecycle evidence artifact key and state/evidence commit boundary

source_evidence.note: Filename identity is generatedAt to milliseconds plus command and outcome; write rejects an existing path.
Scheduler uses the same collision-prone key.
Worker uses the same collision-prone key.
Operator lifecycle evidence has the same timestamp-command-outcome identity.

records.preconditions: Two records for the same command/outcome are generated in one millisecond, the injected clock is fixed/coarse, or concurrent status calls share a timestamp.
records.trigger: Run startup and a fast pass, or two status commands, with the same generatedAt millisecond.
records.expected_behavior: Evidence identity must include a collision-resistant runtime generation and monotonic event sequence/UUID, with atomic no-overwrite publication and deterministic index linkage.
records.current_behavior: The second legitimate event targets the same path and throws. State may already have advanced before evidence publication fails.
records.impact: A fast service can crash on its first pass, concurrent status can fail, and state/evidence diverge. Restart and acceptance trails become incomplete.
records.evidence: The inert convergence harness fixed now() to one timestamp. service_started wrote the first run-running file; pass_completed attempted the same path and threw already exists.

reproduction_status.result: First pass failed because startup and completion resolved to one evidence filename.

records.transaction_or_state_machine_analysis: STATE_WRITTEN -> EVIDENCE_WRITE can fail for a normal event identity collision. There is no atomic aggregate or recovery index to reconcile the advanced state with missing evidence.
records.root_cause: Wall-clock millisecond plus low-cardinality fields is used as a uniqueness key rather than a timestamp attribute.
records.minimal_fix_boundary: Add runtimeId plus a monotonic event counter or UUID to evidence IDs, use atomic create, update an append/index record only after durable artifact publication, and define recovery when state exists without its evidence event.
required_tests: Fixed clock startup plus pass completion
Concurrent status commands
Multiple blocked/retry passes in one millisecond
Clock regression
State/evidence write failure reconciliation
regression_risks: Changing filenames affects evidence indexes, retention, and downstream handoffs
Sequence allocation must itself be concurrency-safe
aliases_or_dependencies: No inherited root cause owns lifecycle evidence filename uniqueness
explicitly_unchanged_areas: Existing no-overwrite check is an intentional safeguard against silent artifact replacement
No repository evidence was written

records.title: Health and failure diagnostics synchronously hash or read unbounded filesystem data
records.relevant_lifecycle_object_or_process: API event loop, startup failure reporting, and root runtime diagnostics

source_evidence.note: Each operational snapshot recursively lists and reads every cockpit asset synchronously to recompute a digest.
Failure-tail logic reads the entire log into memory before selecting the final 20 lines.
Runtime summary synchronously lists and sorts every structured log file without a cap.

records.preconditions: Cockpit assets, child logs, or structured log directories grow large or contain many files.
records.trigger: Query health/readiness repeatedly or trigger startup diagnostics under large filesystem state.
records.expected_behavior: Hot health paths and failure reporting must use bounded cached fingerprints, bounded tail reads, capped file enumeration, and explicit stale/error states.
records.current_behavior: Health recomputes the entire build digest synchronously; error-tail reads full logs; root summary enumerates all matching logs.
records.impact: The loopback API can block, memory can spike during failure handling, status can exceed its own deadlines, and observability work can prevent shutdown.
records.evidence: Static source shows unbounded synchronous reads/enumeration on production request and failure paths. No configured byte/file/depth limits exist.

reproduction_status.result: No finite filesystem workload bound is enforced.

records.transaction_or_state_machine_analysis: Diagnostic and health work is not budgeted as a resource-owned operation. Data growth increases latency and memory without changing configuration.
records.root_cause: Immutable build metadata and bounded tail/index primitives exist conceptually, but production paths recompute or scan raw filesystem content.
records.minimal_fix_boundary: Verify cockpit digest once at startup and cache it with immutable build identity, stream bounded log tails from the end, cap and page log listings, and propagate timeout/stale/error conditions without blocking the event loop.
required_tests: Large cockpit asset tree
Single multi-gigabyte child log
Hundreds of thousands of structured logs
Concurrent health requests
Filesystem mutation/error during scan
regression_risks: Caching must remain bound to immutable asset generation
Bounded tails must preserve redaction and valid UTF-8 handling
aliases_or_dependencies: BWS116-R03-012 owns unbounded database reads, not these filesystem operations
explicitly_unchanged_areas: Current path-containment check for child logs remains unchanged
No large-file stress harness was run to avoid resource abuse

records.title: Configuration mismatch can block emergency management of still-owned processes
records.details: Status and stop fail closed when the current configuration fingerprint differs from recorded state. This prevents accidental cross-configuration control, but the supplied source does not provide a separately authorized recovery path that can stop exact token/start-tick owners without reproducing old configuration. Dynamic operator recovery was not exercised.

records.title: Canonical Node 20.20.2 was unavailable
records.details: Actual Node was v22.16.0. All TypeScript loader tests and inert harness results are supplementary rather than canonical acceptance.

records.title: PostgreSQL execution was unavailable and prohibited without a safe disposable local server
records.details: No psql client or safely configured local PostgreSQL server was present. No database was created, contacted, or mutated. R03 findings remain authoritative for PostgreSQL behavior.

records.title: Clean TypeScript compilation could not run without installing absent dependencies
records.details: The archive has no node_modules and tsc failed on missing @types/node. Dependency installation was prohibited. Global ts-node was used only for bounded supplementary harnesses.

records.title: R01 convergence deadline and late completion
records.details: Retain BWS116-R01-006 and BWS116-R01-007 for upstream pagination/cycle boundedness and underlying convergence late-result ownership. R06 owns only aggregate process lifecycle deadlines and service terminality.

records.title: R01 transport limits and external URL authority
records.details: Retain BWS116-R01-008 and BWS116-R01-009 for response buffering, DNS/redirect and upstream target validation. R06 did not reclassify them.

records.title: R03 concurrent migration ownership
records.details: BWS116-R03-004 remains the owner of migration serialization. R06-001 can make that defect reachable through concurrent service starts.

records.title: R03 psql timeout and cancellation
records.details: BWS116-R03-005 remains the owner of psql subprocess timeout/cancellation. R06 owns propagation of the outer shutdown/deadline state.

records.title: R03 durable transition, lease, fencing and retry mechanics
records.details: BWS116-R03-007 through R03-010 remain authoritative for durable state transitions, lease fencing, caller-controlled lease time and expired-lease retry handling.

records.title: R03 in-flight scheduler and worker cancellation
records.details: BWS116-R03-011 remains the owner of pass and database work that continues after service timeout or shutdown. R06-010 through R06-015 cover process-level shutdown ordering, ownership and terminal state.

records.title: R03 database read boundedness
records.details: BWS116-R03-012 remains the owner of unbounded persistence reads. R06-017 is limited to filesystem/request-path boundedness.

records.title: R05 API and cockpit presentation truth
records.details: R05 should consume R06-007 and R06-008 when judging whether the operator cockpit or read models promote declaration/stale state to green. R06 owns the service-status source and wrapper lifecycle authority.

records.title: R11 assurance and source-manifest drift
records.details: R11 must retain KNOWN_BASELINE_MANIFEST_DRIFT and evaluate why validators/tests accept the R06 lifecycle defects, including synthetic wrapper envelopes and wrong shutdown-order assertions.

records.title: R23 deployment and supervision
records.details: A future deployment/supervision review must consume R06-003, R06-006, R06-009, R06-011, R06-012 and R06-013. R06 owns source behavior; deployment packaging/system integration remains cross-area.

records.title: Strong initial Linux process identity verification
records.details: The lifecycle owner verifies repository cwd, exact command vector, lifecycle token and /proc start ticks before classifying a process running. R06-012 concerns loss of that identity at signal/wait, not the initial check.

records.title: No process-name killing
records.details: Signals target recorded PIDs rather than broad process-name matching.

records.title: Paper-only, provider-disabled and execution-disabled runtime policy
records.details: Reviewed lifecycle paths retain the no-live-operation boundary and loopback API policy.

records.title: Atomic state-file replacement prevents torn JSON
records.details: Temporary write plus rename protects byte integrity. It does not create exclusive ownership, which is R06-001.

records.title: Probe timeout handles are cleared
records.details: fetchProbe uses AbortController and clears its timer in finally. This is distinct from the pass-timer leak in R06-014.

records.title: Direct stop retains state when shutdown throws
records.details: The normal stop path removes state only after shutdownManagedProcesses completes. R06-005 concerns the separate stale-recovery path that suppresses failure and deletes it.

records.title: Evidence files reject silent overwrite
records.details: Evidence writers refuse an existing path. This preserves immutability but exposes the inadequate identity key in R06-016.

records.title: Detached children are not inherently invalid
records.details: Detachment can be acceptable when an exact durable owner, generation, bounded cleanup and supervisor exist. Findings target missing/unsafe ownership transitions, not detachment by itself.

records.title: Automatic restart is not independently required
records.details: The repository may intentionally leave restart to an external supervisor. The defect is false active/readiness and unsafe replacement, not absence of an internal restart loop.

records.title: Blocked external BWS-600 readiness need not abort process startup
records.details: A process may run while external evidence is blocked. It must be represented as started-not-ready rather than terminal successful readiness.

records.title: Configuration mismatch fail-closed behavior is a valid safeguard
records.details: Rejecting arbitrary changed configuration protects ownership. Only the absence of a proven emergency recovery path remains a hypothesis.

records.title: Timestamped immutable evidence is acceptable in principle
records.details: The defect is collision-prone event identity and missing canonical linkage, not the use of timestamps as metadata.

records.title: No real interprocess concurrent-start test
records.details: Focused tests do not launch two OS lifecycle owners or standalone services against one state path.

records.title: No full-role initialization/readiness adversary
records.details: Tests check child presence and accept blocked readiness; they do not hold scheduler, worker, convergence or database initialization in a partial state.

records.title: No active-generation mutation test
records.details: Tests do not start one executable generation, change source/dist/manifest, then run status and stop.

records.title: No startup interruption and failed-cleanup matrix
records.details: There is no adversarial test for each spawn-to-record window, parent signal during initialization, or stale cleanup failure followed by replacement.

records.title: No hung-child and PID-reuse shutdown test
records.details: The process adapter does not model identity change immediately before signal or one child preventing later stop stages.

records.title: Root-wrapper tests use non-production envelopes and fabricated latest files
records.details: The wrapper test server returns top-level status values and writes state/evidence shapes production does not generate.

records.title: No API async-failure/socket-drain test
records.details: Tests do not throw metrics/status/logger callbacks, hold sockets open, race concurrent close calls, or assert application.closed settlement.

records.title: No timer-handle, constant-clock or unexpected-rejection lifecycle test
records.details: Tests do not check losing timer cleanup, same-millisecond evidence IDs, or terminal state after a rejected pass.

records.title: Canonical Node 20/systemd integration remains unexecuted here
records.details: Node 20.20.2 and a safe user-systemd integration environment were unavailable in this review.
